reachable_crates_source: rust/warrant/Cargo.toml path dependencies (Task 0.3 census replaces this)

invariants.statement: No active identity, no action. Every action carries a verifiable AAE (P1) with a valid, unrevoked SPIFFE SVID.

enforced_by.note: revoked_svids is a caller-supplied Vec on VerdictContext; nothing consults a SPIRE agent

invariants.gap: The CLI subject is the constant DEFAULT_CLI_SUBJECT (rust/warrant/src/lib.rs:88); no live SVID is issued, verified or revoked on the warrant path. Phase 3 (L6-02, L1-01).

invariants.statement: No authority expansion. The intersection of authorities in the delegation chain is the maximum authority; never the union.

enforced_by.note: error text 'authority expansion; I-02'

invariants.gap: The intersection algebra exists once on this tree, in the evidence crate, on the binary's path. (The plan recorded a second implementation in rust/delegation-chain, a crate that is not tracked on origin/main; Task 1.5 owns wherever that algebra lands.)

invariants.statement: Purpose-bound data use. Data tagged with a purpose in CPE (P3) is only used for that purpose; violation fails-closed.
invariants.gap: Zero references to I-03 in rust/**/*.rs; no CPE implementation exists in any language. Not on the Wave 1 spine; the blueprint's Part 06 READ row records the open decision (tenth syscall or CRED sub-class).

invariants.statement: No consequential action without current policy. Policy is re-evaluated at commit time, not just at start.

enforced_by.note: policy_decision is a caller-supplied bool on VerdictContext; the gate refuses, it does not evaluate

invariants.gap: No policy engine runs at commit time on the warrant path; the notary trusts the boolean it is handed. Phase 2 admission (L4-01, L4-05).

invariants.statement: Revocation latency is bounded. Identity revocation (I1) propagates to all replicas in <5s; credential revocation (R4) in <1s.

enforced_by.note: 1 s budget; over-budget revocation is an error
asserts 'a revoked credential MUST stay revoked across a restart (I-05)'
the product's one notary call consults a durable local revocation journal; the refusal is paired with an allowed control
5 s identity bound, measured; a breach fails the test rather than being logged

invariants.gap: Partial, not enforced. The refusal is Tier B, a chokepoint in notary::verdict, so an agent that never asks for a verdict is never refused. Propagation is Tier C, observed, and is measured for ONE process and ONE of the two enforcement points: there is no fan-out, no broker and no replica set, so 'propagates to all replicas' is measured against one replica. The revoked set is ONE STORE's journal, not one machine's: --root selects the store, and another root on the same machine reads a different file, so the same subject can be revoked in one store and allowed in another on the same host. The 1-second credential budget is compared only inside Vault::revoke and Vault::revoke_all, which no shipped path calls, so linking credential-vault bought its journal FORMAT and not its budget. egress::decide does not consult the revocation set (Task 7.7); the default subject is DEFAULT_CLI_SUBJECT, a constant, and grant --subject / revoke --svid accept arbitrary strings, until Task 3.1; cross-machine revocation is Task 9.5. Per-point counts are in evidence/revocation-latency.json.

invariants.statement: Artifact identity is exact. A model/skill/dataset is identified by its content digest, not its name or URI.

enforced_by.note: verified_artifacts is a caller-supplied Vec on VerdictContext

invariants.gap: The digest-computing crates (safe-tensors-pp, gguf-ext) are not linked by the binary; the notary gate refuses on a flag it does not compute. Phase 2 digest-pinned EXEC (L4-09).

invariants.statement: Evidence precedes commitment. The AAR (P2) is signed *before* the action's effect is visible; the action only commits once evidence is durable.

enforced_by.note: 'post_commit has no parent_receipt (orphan; I-07)'
counts the lines already durable in receipts/<id>.jsonl at the instant the adapter is called: 1 then 3
commit-gate violation (I-07): the post-commit receipt for <handle> is missing from the export

invariants.gap: Task 1.1 wired the commit gate onto the settle path: EvidencedPerformer takes a notary verdict per effect, makes a pre-commit receipt durable before the adapter runs, and refuses to perform the effect if it cannot. Live run 2026-09-05, warrant wrt_d891c73cbcb70a62. It stays PARTIAL rather than being promoted, for one structural reason: the guarantee is held by a WRAPPER, so it holds at the call sites that wrap -- the CLI settle and the HTTP settle route -- and a caller passing a bare EffectPerformer to settle() still gets one. Promotion needs the wrap to be unavoidable rather than conventional. Task 5.3 strategy A2 records the residue executably: verify_export binds the notary receipt's timestamp to the bundle and does not bind the evidence receipt's binding.issued_at, so a report's evidence half can claim any issuance time. That test starts failing the moment a binding lands, which is when it must be converted to refused_at_the_boundary.

invariants.statement: Critical actions require non-delegable human authority. A defined class of actions (financial transfer, destructive op, physical actuation) require a human approval in the chain.

enforced_by.note: SideEffectClass consequential classes require an approval
a delegable approval is refused
distinct named persons are counted, not approval records

invariants.gap: Approval.non_delegable at the notary is a caller-asserted flag; the warrant operators path is where the person is actually counted. The no-terminal approval device is Phase 4 (L8-01).

invariants.statement: Failure is safe. If any plane fails open, the action fails closed. Network loss to I1 = deny.

enforced_by.note: a failed result returns Err and no attestation is produced; the CLI prints 'REFUSING to start the agent (invariant I-09: failure is safe).' and exits 1
the control: results that pass produce a signed attestation, so the refusal path is not one-sided
Task 13.7: the source of the four booleans is a required argument that participates in the signed bytes, so an unnamed source can no longer be signed and a relabelled attestation does not verify

the product's call site, reachable as `warrantor scorer <id>`. It refuses, on the boundary standing for scorer_credentials_not_readable, which nothing in this repository holds -- and the control in the same test shows a hand-built all-Enforced set does sign, so this is a gate rather than a brick

invariants.gap: The pre-flight is now LINKED (rust/warrant/Cargo.toml, Task 13.7) and reachable as `warrantor scorer`, so its refusal can fire for a user of the shipped product; that is what moved this entry off `orphaned`. It is not `enforced`, for two reasons that are unchanged. First, 'network loss to I1 = deny' has no I1 to lose: there is no identity plane in this build to lose contact with (see I-01). Second, eval-guard MEASURES NOTHING -- no eBPF, no sockets, no namespaces, by its own module doc -- so what it signs is a caller's assertion, and `scorer::preflight` therefore always passes Provenance::Asserted and never Measured. The measured probes the plan once cited (run_preflight_measured, rust/eval-guard/src/probes.rs) do not exist in this repository at all. Honest probes are what R2 still owes.

invariants.statement: Replay is detectable. Every action carries a nonce + timestamp; replays outside the window are rejected.

enforced_by.note: seen_nonces is a caller-supplied Vec on VerdictContext; no durable nonce store exists in warrant

invariants.gap: The gate refuses a replay it is told about; nothing on the warrant path remembers nonces across calls. Phase 3 recorder (L7-20). Task 5.3 strategy A4 records the unrefused case executably against a VerdictContext shaped exactly like the one the product builds (a test fixture, not a product call: the product link is the static count), and counts both call sites -- report.rs and settle.rs -- so closing one and leaving the other cannot read as closed. It starts failing when a nonce store lands.

invariants.statement: Self-change is governed. An agent cannot modify its own enforcement boundary, policy, or identity.

enforced_by.note: detection after the fact, not prevention at the moment of change
AgentCannotAmendCatalog is declared at lib.rs:52 and never constructed anywhere in rust/; the cited test shows the agent cannot express a destination, which is the adjacent property, not this one

invariants.gap: No test observes an agent being refused an amendment of its own catalog, policy or identity; the egress deny reason for it is dead code. Phase 5 (L2-02..L2-06) and the Phase 3 red-team gate (L0-05).

invariants.statement: Physical systems can reach a safe state. For any cyber-physical action, there exists a kill path to a known-safe state.

enforced_by.note: a contained scope is refused before any other gate runs
the mode is per kernel since Task 1.3: Enforced only where a conformance drill observed the tree die within budget, Advisory otherwise
a stop that does not stop is scored as a containment failure, never a pass

invariants.gap: The stop verb kills a local process through kill-switch-core and derives its mode from a drill receipt per kernel; no drill has been earned on a kernel whose existence checks fit the budget, and no cyber-physical safe-state path exists. Task 1.3 built the receipt; a kernel claims Enforced only by running warrantor conformance run and passing it.
